newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine economy minister criticises central bank.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine economy minister criticises central bank.

text.p: Ukraine's new economy minister added his voice to recent government attacks on the policies of the central bank on Wednesday, vowing it would be brought to heel.

"We will force them to work with us. We will force them to sit at our table and talk to us," Yuri Yekhanurov told his first news conference since President Leonid Kuchma appointed him after sacking four ministers on February 25.
"We want central bank policies we can predict, and if it can't fulfil them we should know that too," Yekhanurov said.
But Yekhanurov also praised the bank for taming inflation in the former Soviet republic and introducing a stable currency.

Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko criticised the central bank in parliament this week, indirectly calling for the bank to provide direct credits to the government, after he said there was an insufficient supply of money in the economy.
Bank chief Viktor Yushchenko, whose tight monetary policies have won him a solid reputation with the International Monetary Fund and Western economists, has kept quiet amid the criticism.

Lazarenko, who late last year suggested forming a commission to oversee the bank, also accused it of robbing producers of about $1.3 billion because it failed to adopt a currency corridor or trading band.
The hryvnia, which has been fairly stable since it was introduced at 1.76 to the dollar last year, firmed on Wednesday to 1.8300 from 1.8320 on the Ukraine Interbank Currency Exchange.
Yekhanurov, former chairman of the state privatisation agency, said the bank and government should share similar views.
"We want to find a common language with the central bank. We want to work with it," he said.
Ukraine's inflation is forecast at 24-25 percent this year down from 39.7 percent last year and 181 percent in 1995, but gross domestic product fell 10 percent in 1996.
Yushchenko's re-appointment to a second term last month was overwhelmingly supported by parliament, which under Ukrainian law oversees central bank activities.
